conclusions: The 1 by 1 real matrix [a] is hyperbolic in the encoded sense: it has a real eigenvalue function and a real eigenbasis indexed by Fin 1, with the basis vector satisfying the corresponding eigenvector equation.
mathematical_definitions: The coefficient matrix is the constant function on Fin 1 x Fin 1 with value a, hence the ordinary matrix [a].
Hyperbolicity means existence of a complete real eigenbasis, not a sign or positivity condition.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real scalar speed a, the one-dimensional coefficient matrix [a] has a complete real eigenbasis and is therefore hyperbolic.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement concerns only the one-dimensional, 1 by 1 case.
No sign, nonzero, or boundedness condition on speed is imposed; speed=0 is included.
The existential eigenvalue and eigenbasis are not named or asserted unique, although canonically the eigenvalue is a and any nonzero one-dimensional basis vector works.
The proposition is purely algebraic and contains no scalar PDE solution, characteristic curve, regularity, or propagation statement.
